newsitem.title: THAILAND: Siam Cement says no impact from forex volatility.
newsitem.headline: Siam Cement says no impact from forex volatility.

text.p: Siam Cement Co Plc, Thailand's largest industrial conglomerate, said on Wednesday that recent baht volatility would have no impact on its huge outstanding foreign debts.

Chumpol Na Lamlieng, president of Siam Cement, told reporters that his company's foreign currency borrowings were in line with the central bank's basket of currencies which is the basis for fixing the Thai unit's midrate daily.

"As long as the Bank of Thailand sticks to the basket of currencies the volatility in foreign exchange will have no effect on our foreign debts," he said. "Currently, the company has loans denominated in foreign currencies totalling three billion dollars," he said.
The basket of currencies is heavily weighted in the U.S. dollar, followed by the yen and mark.
"This year's sales growth for Siam Cement will fall to between 5-10 percent compared with an original projection of 15 percent due to the slower economy," Chumpol said.
